title: Solving linear equations involving fractions
competency: Solve linear equations with fractions and recognise equivalent equations.

keywords.def: Least common multiple: the smallest number that all the denominators divide.
Two or more equations that have the same solution.

en.text: To solve an equation with fractions, multiply both sides by the LCM of the denominators. The fractions disappear. Then solve as before. For x/3 + 5 = 7, multiply by 3: x + 15 = 21, so x = 6.

screens.title: Clear the fraction
screens.ask: x/3 + 5 = 7. Which number can you multiply both sides by to remove the fraction?
screens.after: Multiplying by 3 turns x/3 into x: x + 15 = 21, so x = 6.

screens.title: Note
paras: To solve linear equations involving fractions:
Step 1. Find the least common multiple (LCM) of the denominators.
Step 2. Multiply both sides of the equation by the LCM.
Step 3. Solve: variable terms to one side, constants to the other.

screens.title: Solve (x + 2)/4 = 5/3
steps: The LCM of 4 and 3 is 12. Multiply both sides by 12.

screens.title: Why multiply by the LCM?
screens.ask: (x + 2)/4 = 5/3. Tap each card to see what × 12 does.
items: 12 is the smallest number that both 4 and 3 divide.
12 ÷ 4 = 3, so it becomes 3(x + 2). No fraction is left.

screens.title: Solve x/8 + 7/4 = 5/6
steps: The LCM of 8, 4 and 6 is 24. Multiply every term by 24.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Least common multiple: the smallest number that all the denominators divide.

screens.ask: Solve the equation with fractions: x/2 = 5/2. x = ___
screens.why:
Both sides have the denominator 2.
Multiply both sides by 2: x = 5.
Check: 5/2 = 5/2.

screens.ask: Solve the equation with fractions: 3/4 = x/8. x = ___
screens.why:
The LCM of 4 and 8 is 8.
Multiply both sides by 8: 8 × 3/4 = 6 and 8 × x/8 = x.
So 6 = x.
Check: 6/8 = 3/4.

screens.ask: Solve the equation with fractions: 3/4 + x/2 = x/3. x = ___
screens.why:
The LCM of 4, 2 and 3 is 12.
Multiply every term by 12: 9 + 6x = 4x.
Shift: 6x − 4x = −9, so 2x = −9.
x = −9/2 = −4.5.
Check: 0.75 − 2.25 = −1.5 and −4.5 ÷ 3 = −1.5.

screens.ask: Solve the equation with fractions: (7/10)x + 3/2 = (3/5)x + 2. x = ___
screens.why:
The LCM of 10, 2 and 5 is 10.
Multiply every term by 10: 7x + 15 = 6x + 20.
Shift: 7x − 6x = 20 − 15.
x = 5.
Check: 3.5 + 1.5 = 5 and 3 + 2 = 5.

screens.ask: Solve the equation with fractions: (x − 1)/2 + (x + 1)/3 = 4. x = ___
screens.why:
The LCM of 2 and 3 is 6.
Multiply every term by 6: 3(x − 1) + 2(x + 1) = 24.
Remove brackets: 3x − 3 + 2x + 2 = 24.
5x − 1 = 24, so 5x = 25 and x = 5.
Check: 4/2 + 6/3 = 2 + 2 = 4.
screens.clue: Multiply every term by 6, then remove the brackets.

en.text: Equivalent equations have the same solution. 2x − 1 = 11 and x + 12 = 3x both give x = 6, so they are equivalent. To check, solve each one and compare.

screens.title: Same answer?
screens.ask: 2x − 1 = 11 and x + 12 = 3x. Do they have the same solution?
screens.after: Solve each: 2x = 12 gives x = 6, and −2x = −12 gives x = 6. Same solution.

screens.title: Definition 3.11
paras: Equivalent equations are two or more equations that have the same solution.
So these two are not equivalent.

screens.title: Examples 9 and 10
screens.ask: Tap each equation to see its solution.
items: 12 = 2x, so x = 6. Same solution as 2x − 1 = 11: equivalent.
2x = 14, so x = 7. Not the same as x = 16: not equivalent.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Two or more equations that have the same solution.

screens.text: Equivalent equations: true or false? x = 0 and 2x − 1 = −1 are equivalent.
screens.why:
Solve 2x − 1 = −1: add 1, so 2x = 0.
Divide by 2: x = 0.
Both equations give x = 0.
Same solution, so they are equivalent. True.

screens.text: Equivalent equations: true or false? 2x − 6 = 2 and −x = −5 are equivalent.
screens.why:
2x − 6 = 2 gives 2x = 8, so x = 4.
−x = −5 gives x = 5.
4 and 5 are different solutions.
So they are not equivalent. False.

screens.text: Equivalent equations: which equation is equivalent to x = 3?
screens.why:
Solve each choice.
2x = 6 gives x = 3. Same!
x + 3 = 0 gives x = −3.
3x = 1 gives x = 1/3.
Only 2x = 6 is equivalent to x = 3.

screens.text: Equivalent equations: which equation is equivalent to x/2 − 1 = 3?
screens.why:
Solve the given one: x/2 = 4, so x = 8.
x − 2 = 6 gives x = 8. Same!
x − 1 = 6 gives 7.
x = 4 and x/2 = 2 both give 4.
So x − 2 = 6 is equivalent.
screens.clue: Solve the given equation first, then each choice.

screens.title: LCM of 4 and 6
steps: 12 is the first number in both lists.

screens.text: Find the LCM: what is the least common multiple of 3, 4 and 6?
screens.why:
Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, …
6 is not divided by 4.
12 ÷ 3 = 4, 12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 12 ÷ 6 = 2.
So the LCM is 12. (24 and 72 are common multiples, but not the least.)
screens.clue: List multiples of 6 and stop at the first one 3 and 4 divide.

items.ask: Solve the equation with fractions: 5x/13 + 5x/26 = 1. x = ___
items.why:
The LCM of 13 and 26 is 26.
Multiply every term by 26: 10x + 5x = 26.
15x = 26.
x = 26/15 = 1 11/15.

items.ask: Solve the equation with fractions: −3/5 + x/10 = −1/5 − x/5. x = ___
items.why:
The LCM of 5 and 10 is 10.
Multiply every term by 10: −6 + x = −2 − 2x.
Shift: x + 2x = −2 + 6, so 3x = 4.
x = 4/3 = 1 1/3.

items.ask: Solve the equation with fractions: 9w/7 − 6 = 5w/7 + 12. w = ___
Solve the equation with fractions: (7/10)x + 3/2 = (3/5)x + 2. x = ___
items.why:
The LCM of 10, 2 and 5 is 10.
Multiply every term by 10: 7x + 15 = 6x + 20.
Shift: 7x − 6x = 20 − 15.
x = 5.
Check: 3.5 + 1.5 = 5 and 3 + 2 = 5.

items.ask: Solve the equation with fractions: (1/2)(4x + 6) = (1/3)(9x − 24). x = ___
Solve the equation with fractions: (n + 1)/2 + (n + 2)/3 + (n + 4)/4 = 3. n = ___
items.why:
The LCM of 2, 3 and 4 is 12.
Multiply by 12: 6(n + 1) + 4(n + 2) + 3(n + 4) = 36.
Remove brackets: 6n + 6 + 4n + 8 + 3n + 12 = 36.
13n + 26 = 36, so 13n = 10.
n = 10/13.

items.ask: Solve the equation with fractions: (1/3)(x + 6) − (1/2)(3x − 4) = 5. x = ___
items.why:
The LCM of 3 and 2 is 6.
Multiply every term by 6: 2(x + 6) − 3(3x − 4) = 30.
Remove brackets: 2x + 12 − 9x + 12 = 30.
−7x + 24 = 30, so −7x = 6.
x = −6/7.

5x = 10 gives x = 2.
14 = 2x + 4 gives 10 = 2x, so x = 5.
2 and 5 are different.
So they are not equivalent. No.

items.text: Equivalent equations: are x = 0 and 324x + 55 = 55 equivalent?
items.why:
Solve 324x + 55 = 55: subtract 55, so 324x = 0.
Divide by 324: x = 0.
Both give x = 0.
So they are equivalent. Yes.

test.why:
Multiply every term by 3: x + 15 = 21.
Shift 15: x = 21 − 15 = 6.
Check: 6/3 + 5 = 2 + 5 = 7.

test.text: Clear the fractions: to solve x/4 + 1/6 = 2, multiply every term by:
test.why:
The denominators are 4 and 6.
Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, …
Multiples of 6: 6, 12, …
The LCM is 12. (24 also works, but 12 is the least.)

test.ask: Solve the equation with a fraction: (x + 1)/3 = 2. x = ___
test.why:
Multiply both sides by 3: x + 1 = 6.
Shift +1: x = 5.
Check: (5 + 1)/3 = 6/3 = 2.

test.text: Equivalent equations: true or false? 2(x − 5) = x + 6 and 2x − 4 = 10 are equivalent.
test.why:
2(x − 5) = x + 6: 2x − 10 = x + 6, so x = 16.
2x − 4 = 10: 2x = 14, so x = 7.
16 and 7 are different.
Not equivalent. False.
